context: Server health dashboard for 20 servers with interactive threshold sliders that recolor status indicators live; a KPI summary strip (critical/warning/healthy/avg CPU counts), a sortable 7-column table with in-cell sparklines (CPU history), bullet charts (memory), uptime bars, and colored status dots/text — all keyed to two adjustable CPU thresholds.
first_impression: Clean, well-organized operational dashboard that manages substantial per-row complexity through rigorous, consistent color encoding across every visual element.
what_works: The three-color status grammar (green/yellow/red from a colorblind-safe Tol palette) is applied uniformly across status dots, CPU % numerics, bullet chart fills, and sparkline endpoint dots — creating instant pattern recognition without any legend lookup. The KPI strip gives a fleet-level summary before the viewer needs to scan rows, reducing the cognitive overhead of processing 20 rows individually.
what_doesnt: The memory bullet chart applies CPU threshold percentages to memory utilization (e.g., a server is 'critical' on memory if mem_pct >= critThreshold/100), conflating two different resource domains under one threshold control — a viewer adjusting Warning CPU% to 60% would unknowingly reclassify memory status too, creating subtle misreads. The FLIP row-reorder animation on sort cannot be assessed from a static screenshot, so its object-constancy quality is unverifiable.
